summary:
Only the static analysis and the cave assembly source were finished. apply.py, the test file and a --build output were not produced in this session, so nothing was built, no md5 of a patched output exists, and no tests ran.

Static findings from disassembling the carved CShell.dll v3 (SHOGOP3.REZ at 0x2bca8, md5 eb0286632a78bd488bd0f41f37114c4d, PE CheckSum 0; the REZ itself is md5 bd1acfd9cab23d8d0b022a7633340d5a, 1,761,076 B). They confirm the verifier's diagnosis and add to it:

(1) The device record has this layout: +0 description[0x80], +0x80 internal name[0x80], +0x100 and +0x104 HSTRINGs, +0x108 count, +0x10c twelve 16-byte entries (w, h, hstr, hstr). The device constructor at 0x10003a90 zeroes exactly 12 entries. 0x100019c0 builds 4 devices per renderer, stride 0x1cc; renderers have stride 0x7c0 and a cap of 8.

(2) The append at 0x10003546 has no bound. The second pass at 0x10003722 then creates two HSTRINGs per entry, which it writes at entry+8 and entry+0xc. For entries 12..14 those land inside the next device's description at bytes 8..0xf. This is the static cause of the observed '(d3d.ren) Primary X' name, not only of the garbage resolution entries.

(3) 0x10003a00 picks the entry whose HEIGHT is closest to a target. With 1920x1080 in the table, the DISPLAY MODE screen should open on it rather than on 640x480. This is inferred, not proven.

(4) d3d.ren's callback puts each new mode at the front of the list, so the menu order is the reverse of DirectDraw enumeration order. The design therefore does not assume ascending input. When the table is full it removes the smallest-area entry if the new mode is larger, shifts the later entries down to keep their order, and appends. The count is then at most 12 for every input, which is a stronger guarantee than 'shift and keep the last 12'.

(5) On all four LCD boxes the largest mode in the GAMERES list is 1920x1080 (15/16/20/24 modes). So keeping the largest 12 by area keeps 1920x1080, provided the driver offers it at 16 bpp. That is verified on .123 only.

(6) The cave slack at RVA 0x6a315..0x6a3ff (file 0x69715..0x697ff) is all zero. The assembled cave is 0x93 bytes at VA 0x1006a320, and its return jump resolves to 0x1000356c. The plan also sets .text VirtualSize from 0x69315 to 0x69400 so every loader maps the cave.

Still to do before this can be reviewed: the reproducible apply.py (--check/--build/--publish gated on a hardware pass), the relocation and branch-target checks over the detour range, before/after disassembly into the evidence directory, and tests/python/test_patch_shogo.py.
tests: None run. tests/python/test_patch_shogo.py was not written. The only thing checked was that cave.S assembles with i686-w64-mingw32-as into 0x93 bytes (plus 1 byte of objcopy alignment padding) with no relocations, and that the final jump targets 0x1000356c.
risks: The patch is not built. Nothing here may be published.

Two static checks are still undone: that no relocation entry falls in 0x10003546..0x1000356b or in the cave, and that no branch in .text targets the middle of the detour range. Both must be done before any build.
Same-size edit to SHOGOP3.REZ: GAMESYNC only picks it up through the mtime, so publish only through a route that stamps a fresh time (sharewrite.py checks this).
The largest-12 policy drops the smallest modes (640x480 and 800x600 on boxes with more than 12 16-bpp modes). This is intentional, but a player loses the low-resolution options on the default device.
It is unverified whether LithTech caches the extracted CShell.dll between runs, which would mask the patched copy.
Only .123 is proven to offer 1920x1080 at 16 bpp, and d3d.ren lists 16-bpp modes only.
hw_verification_plan:
Once built, use the verifier's proven procedure on .123:
1. Launch with EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\Shogo" "Play Shogo - direct engine.bat" and wait 25 s.
2. Send UIKEY DOWN, DOWN, RETURN (options), RETURN (display), RETURN (change mode), DOWN (resolution), then RIGHT repeatedly. Take up to 5 SCREENSHOTs per step and keep the frame whose max brightness exceeds 200, because the menu text flickers. The menu is keyboard-navigable.
3. PASS needs all of these: '1920 x 1080' appears on the default '(d3d.ren) <card>' device, no numeric garbage entries appear, the list wraps after at most 12 entries, and UP to renderer then RIGHT shows the second device named in full ('Primary Display Driver', not 'Primary X').
4. Apply 1920x1080 once and confirm the fullscreen frame.
5. Exit with taskkill /f /im "Client.exe", then check DISPLAYCFG get and the autoexec.cfg md5.
6. Repeat on .145, .195 and .240.

Must NOT change: the connection to the host's shogo-server. CShell is client-only and the shell-DLL version constant is untouched, but confirm the multiplayer menu still reaches the server list.
review_notes: This session was interrupted before the builder and tests were written, so the result is blocked, not partial-success. The analysis above is ready for whoever finishes the builder. cave.S in the worktree has the entry state, the invariant and the return address documented, and is the reviewable source of the cave bytes. No game data was written into git. No share, box or service was touched.
